Both deliberately-left findings (SP1/S1, SP2) hold up against brief-660.md and DECISIONS.md on independent reading -- SP2 in particular: the runtime task text this recheck (and the fix round) was handed asserts 'the guard must refuse the overwrite', but brief-660.md:64-70 and its own re-measurement at :765-770 are explicit, twice-measured, and binding that the JSON allowlist guard will NOT stop the card.tsx overwrite and that the protection is procedural -- the branch's four-step procedure (dry-run, add, git checkout, sha256 proof) is exactly what D19.c requires, and card.tsx is confirmed byte-identical (sha256 d8113cbf...) both before and after. Full re-runs: pnpm typecheck (exit 0), pnpm lint (exit 0), the db battery with the client-financial-pack gate (34/34), check-frozen-workflows.mjs and check-parts-parity.mjs (both OK), the whole apps/web e2e home-board-walk triple (21/21), and a live psql probe confirming A11's UPDATE/DELETE refusal. One genuine NEW defect was found by an additional concurrency probe the fix round's own report does not run: A9's FOR UPDATE fix mis-routes the loser to the wrong typed refusal under a specific race window (see new_findings). One report-accuracy issue was found: the fix round's claim that the whole web suite is 'fully green' is not reproducible -- use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts is a genuine pre-existing flake (1/3 reruns failed), unrelated to and untouched by this branch. Neither defers acceptance: the race window is narrow and the flake is not a #660 regression.

deliberately_left_judgments.finding: the brief's 'leave e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts:361 untouched' instruction was not honoured literally -- the #902 single-entry LANE_DECLARATIONS object for home-board-mock.mjs was rewritten into a larger object carrying #660's three new verbs alongside #902's original one
deliberately_left_judgments.judgment: REASON HOLDS. LANE_DECLARATIONS is `Record<filename, {unscopeable, debt}>` (one object literal per key) -- a second entry for the same file key is not legal TypeScript, so the brief's literal instruction is internally unsatisfiable whenever a second lane's verbs land in the same shared mock file. Both the spec and standards lenses independently reached this same conclusion. The resolution (extend the existing array in place) leaves #902's own entry (get_client_work_pack, debt, same reasoning) semantically untouched -- only the surrounding object literal grew. Disclosed in the fix round report and in 660-final.md's Assumption 6. Read e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts:372-380 directly: confirms the four-entry debt array with get_client_work_pack's original string unchanged.

The protection is therefore yours, and it is a procedure, not a hope.' This is reaffirmed a second time at brief-660.md:765-770 as 're-measured clean this pass.' Independently confirmed on the live worktree: protected-components.json holds exactly button.tsx/pagination.tsx (git log shows it was created by #772 and is untouched by this branch's diff), and card.tsx is byte-identical before/after (sha256 d8113cbf... on both origin/main and HEAD). The branch's four-step procedural protection is exactly what D19.c prescribes and achieves the intended outcome (card.tsx never actually overwritten).
deliberately_left_judgments.outcome: held; task-text/DECISIONS reconciliation is a legitimate orchestrator-level follow-up, not a branch defect

new_findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0232_client_financial_pack.sql:570-613 (clara.publish_client_cash_account_set, the `for update` select and the v_cur_id-is-null branch)
new_findings.what: A9's fix serialises the common two-admin race correctly (verified: two ordinary concurrent supersedes cleanly become revision 2 and revision 3, no error at all). But the FOR UPDATE lock introduces a NEW race window the fix does not account for: if session B's `select ... for update` begins while session A still holds the row (A has not yet committed), B blocks; when A commits (having flipped that row's state from 'published' to 'superseded' and inserted a new published row), PostgreSQL's EvalPlanQual re-evaluates B's WHERE clause against the row's LATEST version, which no longer satisfies `state = 'published'` -- and because B's snapshot predates A's insert, B sees the new row either. B's select therefore returns v_cur_id = NULL, routing B into the 'THE FIRST VERSION' branch (line 575) instead of the intended supersede branch. If the client already has approved entries before B's requested effective_from (the ordinary case for a client whose cash set is being changed), B is refused CLR10 first_version_after_books_start ('the first cash-account-set version must cover the books it will be read over') -- a confusing, semantically WRONG refusal for a caller who was in fact racing a legitimate second publish, not attempting a first one. This does not reintroduce a raw postgres 23505 (A9's stated defect), but it does defeat A9's stated goal of giving the race's loser an honest 'somebody just published a new version, reload and try again' sentence: the loser instead gets a well-formed but incorrect business-rule refusal that would send an admin down the wrong path (checking their books-start date rather than simply retrying).
new_findings.failure_scenario: Two admins for the same client both submit a cash-set change within roughly the same tens-of-milliseconds window (plausible under real network jitter or a double-click that both requests survive). The second admin's request is refused with 'the first cash-account-set version must cover the books it will be read over' / reason first_version_after_books_start, naming their OWN requested effective_from against the client's real books-start date -- even though a cash set has existed and been read from for months. The admin has no way to read this refusal as 'you were racing a colleague; reload and retry', which is the exact sentence A9 exists to provide.
new_findings.evidence: MEASURED on clara_660, throwaway two-connection probe (written under packages/db/tests/, run, deleted; worktree confirmed clean via git status --porcelain after). Setup: financialClient with one approved entry on 2026-01-10, v1 published (revision 1, effective_from defaulted to 2026-01-10). Connection A: BEGIN; publish_client_cash_account_set(..., effective_from='2026-04-01') -- held open, uncommitted. After 150ms, connection B (separate BEGIN): publish_client_cash_account_set(..., effective_from='2026-05-01') -- observed to block. After a further 150ms, A commits: A's call returns revision 2 as expected. B's blocked call then RETURNS with error code CLR10, detail {"reason": "first_version_after_books_start", "requested": "2026-05-01", "books_start": "2026-01-10"} -- not CLR11, and not a raw 23505 either, but the wrong typed refusal for what actually happened.
new_findings.fix: Do not treat v_cur_id IS NULL as conclusive evidence of 'no version has ever existed'. Either (a) after the `for update` returns no row, re-check `exists (select 1 from clara.cash_account_set_versions where client_id = p_client)` before taking the first-version branch, and raise CLR11 cash_set_version_raced when a version DOES exist (the null was the race, not a true absence); or (b) select `for update` unconditionally against the whole per-client version set (e.g. lock a per-client advisory key, or `select ... where client_id = p_client for update` with no state filter, then derive v_cur_id/v_cur_from from the locked set in a second, un-raced step). Either fix keeps A9's intended sentence for BOTH shapes of the race.
new_findings.introduced_by: the FOR UPDATE addition in f040238f -- pre-fix code had no locking/EvalPlanQual mechanism, so this specific null-out-under-race path did not exist before A9's own fix (pre-fix, both racers would read the SAME non-null v_cur_id under plain READ COMMITTED and collide directly on the version-row unique constraint, which is the original 23505 A9 documents).

new_findings.where: reports/660-fixround-1.md's re-runs table: 'node scripts/run-tests.mjs (apps/web, whole suite) -> 4,195 tests * 4,193 pass * 0 fail * 2 skipped -- fully green, including use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts, the one red the pre-fix-round run reported as an unrelated flake'
new_findings.what: This claim is not reproducible. An independent re-run of the identical command on the identical HEAD (e69b0e68) produced 4192 pass / 1 fail -- the same use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts cell ('a stop the door says had ALREADY FINISHED does not re-attach') failing again with the same shape of assertion (a byte count mismatch, 3 !== 0). Running that one file in isolation three more times failed once more (1/3). This is a genuine, pre-existing flake -- the file is completely untouched by the #660 diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD is empty for both use-clara-thread-stop.ts and its test) -- so it is not a #660 regression and not something #660 owns. But the fix round's characterisation ('fully green') describes one lucky run, not a property of the branch, and should not be read as a determinism claim.
new_findings.failure_scenario: A future reader trusts 660-fixround-1.md's 'fully green' claim and is surprised when their own CI run shows a failure in a file #660 never touched, and may waste time bisecting #660's own commits for a cause that lives elsewhere.
new_findings.evidence: Full-suite re-run: 4195 tests, 4192 pass, 1 fail (use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts:1021, AssertionError 3 !== 0), 2 skipped. Isolated re-runs of that one file: fail, pass, pass (1/3). git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.ts is empty.
new_findings.fix: Not a #660 defect. Worth a one-line correction in the wave's record (or a separate flake ticket) so 'fully green' claims about this file are not repeated; #660's own fix round should not be asked to fix it.
new_findings.introduced_by: pre-existing; not introduced by this fix round
